articles.title: Can the QoS burst defaults on FSx for ONTAP be changed from ONTAP 9.19.1, the same as on-premises? I checked on a live file system
articles.excerpt: Conclusion first: on Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP you can change the QoS burst defaults. Not only is the configuration accepted — a brief overshoot above the ceiling (the burst) happened exactly as con…
articles.body: Conclusion first: on Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP you can change the QoS burst defaults. Not only is the configuration accepted — a brief overshoot above the ceiling (the burst) happened exactly as configured. The catch: you cannot change this setting from the AWS Management Console or the AWS CLI (the AWS API). FSx for ONTAP has two ways in — the AWS-side consoles and APIs, and a separate path that drives the storage engine (ONTAP) directly through its own REST API / CLI. The QoS burst can be set only from that second path. What this post covers, and what it does not A colleague at NetApp asked me, "since ONTAP 9.19.1 you can change the QoS burst defaults (burst-percent / burst-duration / burst-iops), but is that possible on FSx for ONTAP too?" — so I tried it.

articles.title: Running Pandoc in the Browser: WebAssembly, Web Workers, and a 58 MB Module
articles.excerpt: Every "convert my document" tool I've tried has the same shape: you pick a file, it uploads somewhere, a server does the work, you get a download link back. That's fine for public data. It's a much wo…
articles.body: Every "convert my document" tool I've tried has the same shape: you pick a file, it uploads somewhere, a server does the work, you get a download link back. That's fine for public data. It's a much worse deal when the file is a contract, a manuscript, a medical record, or anything else you'd rather not hand to a stranger's S3 bucket. So I built a Word→Markdown converter that never uploads anything. It runs the real Pandoc engine, compiled to WebAssembly, inside a browser tab. Here's what that actually took. Why Pandoc, and not an HTML pipeline The obvious approach for .docx → Markdown is to parse the OOXML into HTML and then walk the HTML into Markdown. That's what most library-based solutions do, and it works for simple documents.

articles.title: Why Windows Battery Life Estimates Don't Match Your Real Runtime
articles.excerpt: A Windows battery report might suggest five hours of battery life, while a coding session lasts closer to two. That difference does not, by itself, prove that the battery is faulty. The useful distinc…
articles.body: A Windows battery report might suggest five hours of battery life, while a coding session lasts closer to two. That difference does not, by itself, prove that the battery is faulty. The useful distinction is stored energy versus power demand . Battery capacity describes one side of that relationship. Your workload determines the other. I run Battery Health Lab. This walkthrough focuses on interpreting the estimates table, not selling a replacement battery or treating one number as a diagnosis. Generate a fresh report Open PowerShell in Windows Terminal as administrator and run: powercfg /batteryreport /output " $ env : USERPROFILE \battery-report.html" Open the HTML file at the location printed by the command, then find Battery life estimates near the bottom.

articles.title: Doze Sort: let a local model file the notes, and keep the originals
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady. I built Doze Sort for a small pile of notes with filenames like note-03.md. Opening each file to decide whe…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady . What I Built I built Doze Sort for a small pile of notes with filenames like note-03.md . Opening each file to decide where it belongs is the part I wanted to hand off. The app uses an open-weight model to compare the contents with topic descriptions. It makes a plan first. After I inspect that plan, one batch action creates copies in the proposed folders. A low score or close result goes to _review . Exact byte duplicates point to one canonical copy. I chose to keep the original pile. That means this is an organized working copy, not a tool that empties a messy folder. It also means a bad category does not lose the source note. Undo moves the completed run into recovery and retains its files.

Generative AI (GenAI) Generative AI is a tool that creates text, code, or answers based only on what you ask it to type. Originally, Kratos was called “Dominus,” which Jaffe liked because it made him sound dominant and strong. Unfortunately, it also made him sound like a chain of pizza restaurants. “The people on the team started making Domino’s Pizza jokes,” Jaffe said . “Every single time someone said Dominus, someone inevitably would yell out, ‘30 minutes or free,’ or, ‘Get the door, it’s Dominus.’ “After about the 50th time, the writing was on the wall.

articles.title: NASA closes the book on epic OSIRIS-REx asteroid-sampling mission: 'I am immensely proud of what we did'
articles.excerpt: NASA's OSIRIS-REx asteroid-sampling mission formally ended on Sept. 30, 2026, though scientists will continue to study the pieces of space rock it returned for decades.
articles.body: On Sept. 30, NASA formally concluded OSIRIS-REx, the historic first U.S. mission to pluck a pristine piece of an asteroid and deliver it safely back to Earth. The van-sized OSIRIS-REx spacecraft — whose name is short for Origins, Spectral Interpretation, Resource Identification, Security-Regolith Explorer — visited and sampled Bennu , an ancient space rock holding pristine remnants from the dawn of our solar system more than 4.5 billion years ago. Among those cosmic relics are raw organic building blocks , the kind that may have seeded life on Earth. "I have known this day was coming for a long time, but it is still difficult to see it arrive," OSIRIS-REx Principal Investigator Dante Lauretta, who's based at the University of Arizona, said in a post on LinkedIn .

articles.body: President Donald Trump announced this afternoon that Elon Musk's SpaceX shares for children will be given through Trump Accounts. Musk said earlier today that he would give one of his SpaceX shares to "every kid in America" sometime next year. Musk had thanked Trump Account booster Brad Gerstner for "helping enable this," and Trump appeared to confirm the plan in a post on Truth Social . Given the value of SpaceX's stock on Friday, 72 million shares would be worth approximately $10.5 billion, according to CNBC . "This will be the first of many," Musk said. articles.title: New 'Blade Runner 2099' trailer is a space fan's dream with sinister starships and strange exoplanets (video)
articles.excerpt: 'More human than human. That's not a slogan; it's a shackle'
articles.body: Cue the depressing rain, dark trench coats, and a dire dystopian dirge because the Blade Runner 2099 trailer is here! Cyberpunk is charging back in confident fashion with Prime Video's latest detour into the neon-drenched dystopia of humans and rogue replicants first introduced in director Sir Ridley Scott's "Blade Runner" from 1982, then revisited in Denis Villeneuve's "Blade Runner 2049." Arriving Nov. 25, 2026, " Blade Runner 2099" 's plot turns the tables as resentful artificial beings are now the ones running the show and hunting down Earth’s humans after a successful uprising against their original makers. This newest atmospheric trailer was unveiled at last week’s New York Comic-Con and has us totally jacked to re-immerse ourselves in that noirish futuristic realm.

articles.title: “We were looking at it wrong”: The explosive claim that’s upended the AI world
articles.excerpt: “I think I have good news about the nature of neural networks.” With those simple words of optimism, Nick Cammarata, a researcher at the AI startup Goodfire, kicked off a 26,000-word blog post that ha…
articles.body: “I think I have good news about the nature of neural networks.” With those simple words of optimism, Nick Cammarata, a researcher at the AI startup Goodfire, kicked off a 26,000-word blog post that has knocked the AI world on its head, sparking wild speculation as well as cautious (and not-so-cautious) celebration. Cammarata’s claim is that LLMs might in fact be far easier to understand—and thus to monitor and control—than people previously thought. If true (and we’ll come back to that), it’s a huge deal.
